holidays.name: National Kindergarten Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the joys of early childhood learning, finger painting, nap time, and the magic of sharing crayons. Grown-ups are encouraged to channel their inner five-year-old.
holidays.origin: Celebrated on the birthday of Friedrich Fröbel, the German educator who founded the first kindergarten in 1837 and coined the word, which means 'children's garden' in German.
holidays.funFact: Fröbel designed a set of play materials called 'Fröbel Gifts,' including wooden blocks and balls, which later inspired architects such as Frank Lloyd Wright.

holidays.name: Tolkien Week Begins (Hobbit-Friendly Spring Celebrations)
holidays.description: Fans of Middle-earth embrace second breakfasts, pipe-weed-free picnics, and marathon viewings of fantasy epics around this time. Pointy ears and hairy feet are optional but encouraged.
holidays.origin: An unofficial fan observance tied to the spring season and to the founding of Rome legend on April 21, which Tolkien fans have long linked to Middle-earth lore and the 'Shire Reckoning' calendar.
holidays.funFact: Tolkien invented the Shire calendar, in which every month has exactly 30 days, and a couple of extra holidays fall outside the months entirely.

holidays.name: National Chocolate-Covered Cashew Truffle Day
holidays.description: A day for indulging in crunchy, buttery cashews wrapped in rich chocolate truffle goodness. Perfect for snackers who want their nuts and their dessert in one bite.
holidays.origin: One of America's many food-based observances created by food enthusiasts and promoters, listed on food-holiday calendars for April 21.
holidays.funFact: Cashews are technically seeds that grow on the outside of a fruit called the cashew apple, and their shells contain a toxin related to poison ivy, so they are never sold raw in the shell.

holidays.name: Rome's Birthday (Natale di Roma)
holidays.description: Italians and history buffs celebrate the legendary founding of Rome with parades, gladiator reenactments, toga-clad festivities, and plenty of pasta.
holidays.origin: According to Roman legend, Romulus founded the city on April 21, 753 BC. The ancient festival of Parilia was celebrated on this day, and the city still marks it with events.
holidays.funFact: During the ancient Parilia festival, Romans jumped over bonfires made of burning straw to purify themselves and their livestock.

holidays.name: Grilled Cheese Sandwich Day (Unofficial Spring Edition)
holidays.description: Cheese lovers gather to celebrate the gooey, golden, crispy comfort of a perfectly grilled cheese sandwich, with extra points for dunking it in tomato soup.
holidays.origin: Observed informally by foodies and social media fans, who celebrate grilled cheese on April 12 officially but often extend the party around mid-to-late April with 'National Grilled Cheese Month.'
holidays.funFact: April is National Grilled Cheese Month in the US, and Americans consume millions of grilled cheese sandwiches each year.
